title: When illness comes
hookLine: patience and seeking treatment: Allah sent no disease without a cure (Bukhari)
tomorrow: the house is quiet tonight. how close is close?

lines: A CUFF STILL IN ITS BOX.
cards: A blood pressure cuff, still in its box. A follow-up appointment, moved twice. Allah decides, someone says, and it's hard to argue with, because to a believer it's true.

So why sit in a waiting room at all? It's an old question. One day some Bedouins, desert Arabs, came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him the plain version, no decoration: Messenger of Allah, should we seek treatment?

teach.b: Two answers live inside the tradition, and both are serious. The first: seek the cure.

teach.h: THE CURE IS FROM ALLAH TOO.
teach.b: In Abu Dawud's report, the Prophet answers the Bedouins: yes, servants of Allah, seek treatment, for Allah made no disease without making a cure for it, except one: old age.
Sahih al-Bukhari has it short: Allah sent down no disease without sending down its cure. Muslim adds that when the cure meets the disease, it heals by Allah's permission.
So the doctor isn't a rival to trust. The cure comes from the same place the illness does. The Prophet had cupping himself, a treatment of his time, and paid the man who did it.
And there's the camel: tie it, he told a man, and trust. Now the second answer, at its strongest.
Bukhari also tells of people who enter paradise without a reckoning: they don't ask for ruqya, healing recitation, or for branding with fire, and they rely on their Lord.

Some scholars read that as praise for a heart so given to God that it lets certain treatments go. Others answer that he praised the trust, not the refusing, since he sought treatment and told others to.

teach.h: BOTH: TRUST LIVES IN THE HEART.
teach.b: Both views meet in one place: tawakkul, trust, lives in the heart.
The first view simply adds that the heart can trust while the hands make the appointment.

how: Muslims generally see medicine as compatible with trust in God: they see doctors and take treatment while making du'a for healing, and some also use ruqya, recitation from the Qur'an over the sick.

o: sickness met with treatment and trust together
sickness as a test you bear without any help
sickness that only du'a, not medicine, heals

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: the one he said has no cure

s: seeing a doctor shows weak trust in Allah
the Prophet told people to seek treatment and had cupping himself.
in one report the Prophet named old age as the illness with no cure
seek treatment, he said, for Allah made a cure for every disease except old age.
every scholar reads the hadith of the trusting people the same way
some read it as praising those who leave certain treatments; others say it praises trust, not refusing.

games.q: your uncle says taking his blood pressure pills shows weak tawakkul. what's the strongest answer from inside the tradition?
o: the Prophet told people to seek treatment and used it himself; the cure is from Allah too.
tawakkul is only a heart thing, so pills and faith have nothing to do with each other.
he's right that trust is higher, but pills are fine for people whose faith is weaker.
games.why: seek treatment, servants of Allah: the cure heals by His permission. even the view that praises leaving some treatments praises the trust, not the danger.

practice: Bring to mind one health thing you've been putting off: a checkup, a refill, a tooth, a worry you haven't said out loud. Name what you'd want, then what's in the way, then one small step and when.
If you pray, you can ask for the cure and for the courage to go get it.

wordCard.voice: When illness comes: seek the cure. The Prophet said Allah sent no disease without one, and the cure heals by His permission.

orig.note: Arabic: remedy, cure. 'for every disease there is a remedy' (Muslim).

carryVoice: Keep this one: seek the cure, and trust the One who sent it down. Go gently.

sources.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud 3855 (Bedouins: should we seek treatment? yes, servants of Allah; a cure for every disease except old age)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5678 (Allah sent down no disease without sending down its cure)
Sahih Muslim 2204 (for every disease a remedy; it heals by Allah's permission)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2103 (the Prophet was cupped and paid the cupper)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5705 (those who enter paradise without reckoning: no ruqya requested, no cautery, they rely on their Lord)
